customer_name: Universidad de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria
business_problem: An aging on-premises AD FS deployment suffered outages and could not provide the security, multifactor authentication, single sign-on, and device-management capabilities the university needed across its distributed campuses.
solution_summary: ULPGC migrated federated identity from on-premises Active Directory Federation Services to Microsoft Entra ID to stop outages and extend secure access across six campuses and three islands. The rollout moved priority applications to the cloud in stages, introduced a preproduction validation environment, then cut over production identity services with partner support. Entra ID now serves as the control plane for Microsoft 365 and other applications, supplying single sign-on, multifactor authentication, conditional access, risk-based policies, and modern device-management foundations. Instead of maintaining redundant local AD FS servers and coping with certificate renewals and availability incidents, the university manages tens of thousands of identities in a simpler cloud service with better resilience, lower infrastructure overhead, and stronger cybersecurity.

solution_components.name: Microsoft Entra ID
solution_components.role: Provides the cloud identity plane for SSO, MFA, conditional access, adaptive policies, and identity management across university applications.

solution_components.name: Microsoft 365
solution_components.role: Acts as a critical downstream productivity and collaboration workload that depends on the new identity layer.

data_flow: User identities authenticate through Microsoft Entra ID, which applies MFA and conditional-access policies before granting single sign-on access to Microsoft 365 and other university applications across campuses and partner environments.
integration_points: Legacy Active Directory Federation Services environment
business_outcome: The university improved service availability and cybersecurity while reducing infrastructure and maintenance costs, giving students, staff, and administrators more reliable access to online services.
metrics: Tens of thousands of identities across multiple applications
architecture_clues: Migration was validated in a preproduction Entra ID environment before production cutover
Two-factor authentication was introduced during the first migration stage
Identity-based and risk-based adaptive access policies are part of the design
evidence_quotes: When an aging on-premises Active Directory Federation Services implementation began experiencing incidents, the university knew it had to move to the cloud.
The solution also simplifies single sign-on, allowing quick access to hybrid and multicloud environments.
With Microsoft Entra ID, the university has gained multifactor authentication, conditional access, and device management alongside a substantial simplification of its infrastructure at a lower cost.
